item.title: Typical Superpositions are Magical
item.description: arXiv:2610.22476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The non-stabilizerness, or "magic", of a quantum state is a common metric for the hardness of simulation on a classical computer, and is often quantified by the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE). We show how random superpositions of classically simulable states saturate the SRE to the symmetry-restricted Haar-random maximum. For any large-$N$ random pure-state ensemble satisfying the conditions of Schur's lemma, the average SRE of the $m$-component superposition $\langle M_2(m)\rangle=N-\log_2[\langle W(m)\rangle]$ is governed by an average witness $\langle W(m)\rangle$ that universally decomposes into a Haar floor and an ensemble-specific excess. As the number of components $m$ increases, the excess is suppressed, resulting in a logarithmic scaling of the SRE before plateauing at the Haar-valued maximum. We derive a general closed form for $\langle W(m)\rangle$ in the thermodynamic limit, and numerically verify our result for random stabilizer states and random Gaussian states.
item.dc:creator: Joshuah T. Heath, Andrew Urilyon, Damien Quinn, Graham Kells

item.title: Exploring Quantum Phase Transitions Beyond Landau Theory on a Quantum Processor
item.description: arXiv:2610.22482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct continuous quantum phase transitions between phases that break distinct symmetries challenge the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and provide a framework for deconfined quantum criticality. Here, we investigate a Landau-forbidden ferromagnetic-to-valence-bond-solid (FM-VBS) transition in a frustrated one-dimensional spin chain using superconducting quantum processors. Combining matrix-product-state-assisted circuit preparation with quantum-hardware measurements, we resolve the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic correlations and the redistribution of competing-order fluctuations across the transition. Distance-resolved correlations and finite-size analyses reveal signatures consistent with critical behavior. We further extend our investigation to nonequilibrium dynamics, directly preparing dimerized states and tracking the evolution of VBS order and joint FM-VBS fluctuations under local unitary interactions. Our results establish a versatile quantum-hardware framework for probing competing orders, critical correlations, and many-body dynamics beyond conventional Landau theory.
item.dc:creator: Ruizhe Shen, Yin Zhong, Ching Hua Lee

item.title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.22489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.
item.dc:creator: Kaumudibikash Goswami, Archana Barvar, Manabendra Nath Bera

item.title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.22532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning $\Delta(t)$ and Rabi frequency $\Omega(t)$ at frequencies $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2=\nu \omega_1$ respectively with $\nu \in \mathbf{Z}$. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$, and $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$ initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.
item.dc:creator: Tista Banerjee, K. Sengupta

item.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.
item.dc:creator: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin, Ryan Thorngren

item.title: Circuit Synthesis for Variational Quantum Algorithms: The Depth of Algebra and Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.22689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The analysis of Hamiltonian Variational Ans\"atze centers on three fundamental questions: which states are exactly reachable from a given initial state, what native control depth suffices for local and global synthesis, and whether a bounded circuit extension can expose a direction of decreasing cost at a suboptimal output. We address these challenges by leveraging the dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) associated with the circuits and the geometry of the initial state's orbit under the action of the corresponding dynamical Lie group $G$. We show that an initial state has a closed projective orbit whenever it is a nondegenerate eigenstate of a control Hamiltonian. Combined with asymptotic QAOA convergence, this guarantees exact, finite depth ground state preparation for architectures employing diagonal problem Hamiltonians and irreducible stoquastic mixers. We bound the number of native control exponentials required for local unitary synthesis and state preparation using DLA commutator filtration growth alongside reachable orbit dimensions. Complementing these local results, we construct global frameworks on invariant sectors equipped with full unitary or special unitary dynamical Lie algebras. These constructions yield explicit applications to Pauli-generated systems and constrained maximum independent set multi-angle QAOA circuits; specifically, we show that their native control costs are directly determined by commutator filtration depth and independent-set toggle-group geometry, respectively. Finally, if the dynamical Lie group is compact, the observable $H_P$ generates an admissible evolution ($iH_P \in \mathfrak{g}$, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is the DLA), and the projective orbit of the initial state contains a ground state ray of $H_P$, then a bounded depth, identity-initialized circuit extension exhibits either first-order descent or negative curvature at every suboptimal circuit output.
item.dc:creator: Boris Tsvelikhovskiy

item.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter-shift rule. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Florencio D\'iaz, Julio Guerrero Garc\'ia, Elvira Romera Guti\'errez

item.title: Metric and Dispersive Dynamics of Phase Perturbations in Bohmian Quantum Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By linearizing the hydrodynamic equations associated with the Madelung transformation in the context of Bohmian dynamics, we derive an effective metric for the phase perturbation around a background state. We show that the metric previously obtained previously by the same authors arises naturally as a particular case of a more general structure, in which the complete functional variation of the quantum potential is retained and external classical potentials can be incorporated. This generalization preserves the dependence of the quantum potential on the density and its spatial derivatives, generating additional terms that introduce dispersive corrections and act as sources in the effective Klein-Gordon equation. To organize these contributions, we introduce differential operators that separate the local sector responsible for the effective geometry from the corrections associated with the complete functional structure of the quantum potential. We identify the conditions under which these additional terms become negligible, recovering homogeneous propagation and the effective geometry for the Gaussian wave packet of a free particle.
item.dc:creator: Felipe S. Esc\'orcio, Hermano Velten

item.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
item.description: arXiv:2610.22738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway itself becomes programmable via tailored excitations. The superlattices host a multiband manifold of co localized topological interface modes, while coherently controlled inputs synthesize pump superpositions within this protected basis. We showcase this principle by selectively addressing topological biphoton eigenstates, steering correlations to produce a desired target state in a high-dimensional Hilbert space, and inverse-designing pump states that generate targeted Schmidt dimensionalities. Site-resolved two-photon correlation measurements remain reproducible across nominally identical fabricated devices, demonstrating robustness to realistic nanofabrication-induced disorder. Programmable preparation of topological entangled states establishes a pathway towards exploiting topological photonic modes as application-specific quantum resources, enabling tailored input states for high-dimensional quantum communication, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing.
item.dc:creator: M. Javad Zakeri, Alaric Pan, Darren D Hudson, Andrea Blanco-Redondo

item.title: The Classical Boundary of Quantum Computation: History-Resolved Causal Stochastic Machines and the Cost of Classicalization
item.description: arXiv:2610.22750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What separates quantum computation from classical computation when a classical model may retain every branch history and arbitrary causal memory? We study this question using history-resolved causal stochastic machines (HCSMs), which describe positive causal history laws. Probabilistic Turing machines (PTMs) embed in stochastic-ensemble models (SEnMs), which in turn embed in HCSMs. We prove that HCSM history laws coincide exactly with the fixed-basis, prefix-preserving diagonal sector of ideal quantum processes, denoted by $\mathsf{PTM}_{\rm proc}$ and distinguished here from algorithmic quantum Turing machines (QTMs). Coherent quantum processes extend strictly beyond this sector. The boundary is already visible in reversibility. Born-probability shadows of unitary gates preserve inverse composition exactly for basis permutations with phases. Outside this class, an exact positive stochastic simulation that supports universal quantum continuations must retain predictive information absent from visible probabilities. An inverse-recovery identity quantifies this phase ledger, and universal continuation forces the retained probability law to be tomographically sufficient for the quantum state. Under continuous full-state encoding assumptions, this requirement yields quantum-state dimension lower bounds. The familiar slogan $\mathsf{PTM}\subseteq\mathsf{QTM}$ is thereby sharpened into a precise classical boundary and a no-free-classicalization principle. Complete classical branching does not remove the predictive information needed to represent quantum coherence.
item.dc:creator: Kyoungho Cho, Junghee Ryu, Minsu Kim, Jeongho Bang

item.title: Quantumness of Entanglement in Schwarzschild de Sitter Spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2610.22761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality of a noisy generalized GHZ state in Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime. The genuine multipartite concurrence and optimized Svetlichny parameter are employed to characterize these two quantum correlations. It is shown that the black hole and cosmological event horizons redistribute genuine multipartite entanglement differently among the physically accessible and inaccessible reduced states, while Svetlichny violation occurs only in the physically accessible state. We find that genuine multipartite entanglement can survive in the physically inaccessible states even when genuine tripartite nonlocality is absent. In addition, initial white noise suppresses both correlations, with Svetlichny nonlocality surviving over a narrower parameter region. Furthermore, in the Nariai limit, under the normalization adopted here, the correlations become concentrated in the physically accessible state. These results demonstrate the different robustness of genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality under horizon effects and initial noise.
item.dc:creator: Sumeng Wang, Xiaofen Huang

item.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.22823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.
item.dc:creator: Will Cavendish

item.title: Quantum approximate stochastic combinatorial optimisation
item.description: arXiv:2610.22876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation concerns discrete decisions made before all relevant information is known. An initial decision is made; once uncertainty is resolved, it can be adapted to the realised scenario, at a cost. The aim is to find the initial decision that minimises the upfront cost plus the expected cost of optimal adaptation. The first-stage decision problem is often NP-hard, and computing the expected minimum recourse cost can be $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard for a single first-stage candidate. We introduce Quantum Approximate Stochastic Combinatorial Optimisation (QASCO), a variational quantum-walk ansatz that coherently incorporates scenario-dependent recourse into its dynamics to search over first-stage decisions without explicitly evaluating expected minimum recourse costs. We demonstrate QASCO for MaxCut with stochastic edge weights, obtain a circuit with polynomial per-layer gate complexity, and study the ansatz via exact state-vector simulation. Across the instances considered, QASCO concentrates amplitude more effectively on stochastic-optimal first-stage decisions than a previously proposed two-stage QAOA construction. We further show that the ansatz can be calibrated using a depth-independent number of parameters and applied to unseen instances without further circuit-parameter optimisation, including joint decision--scenario--recourse spaces spanning more than $2^{32}$ configurations. Under a query-cost model, comparison with the tested classical heuristics using sample-average approximations of the expected minimum recourse cost shows that QASCO more reliably reaches globally optimal first-stage solutions while requiring fewer cut evaluations. These results show how to incorporate scenario-dependent recourse into the ansatz dynamics, providing a general framework for variational quantum walks in two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation.
item.dc:creator: Edric Matwiejew, Paulo E. Santos, Jingbo B. Wang, Ugo Varetto

item.title: Quantum-Assisted Unambiguous Discrimination of Pure States with Robustness Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical framework for the unambiguous discrimination of pure states by combining the noisy intermediate-scale quantum semidefinite program solver (NSS) with the reciprocal-state representation. In NSS, a given semidefinite program (SDP) is represented within a subspace spanned by chosen ansatz states, with the required quantities estimated using quantum circuits, and the resulting optimization is performed classically. This makes NSS naturally applicable to discrimination problems involving circuit-prepared states, as finding a discrimination measurement can be formulated as an SDP. By choosing the discriminated states themselves as the ansatz and exploiting the reciprocal-state representation, the general matrix-variable NSS formulation is reduced to an optimization over N scalar variables, where N is the number of discriminated states. The resulting formulation reduces the number of optimization variables and positive-semidefinite constraints compared with the original NSS formulation. We further establish robustness guarantees against Gram matrix estimation errors, including a rescaling procedure that guarantees a valid positive operator-valued measure (POVM) under bounded perturbations. The resulting bounds quantify both the deviation in average success probability and violations of the no-error condition using only the estimated Gram matrix, its SDP solution, and a characterized perturbation bound, without access to the ideal Gram matrix. Numerical simulations validate the derived robustness bounds and characterize finite-shot scaling. We also perform experiments on IBM quantum hardware to estimate pairwise overlaps, and then evaluate the performance of the resulting POVMs.
item.dc:creator: Jinhyeok Heo, Dongkeun Lee, Junghee Ryu, Minjin Choi

item.title: Encodings and Node Architecture: Lessons from the Fault-Tolerant Distributed Transversal Fanout
item.description: arXiv:2610.22966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An encoding choice specifies the quantum error-correcting code used to encode logical qubits at a given node. Different encoding choices may differ in the number of physical qubits, the number of encoded logical qubits, the code distance, and the available fault-tolerant operations. We study different encodings for a distributed transversal fanout operation and look at its implications on node architecture. Our experiments suggest that an encoding with higher distance, even if requiring more ebits, can yield a lower logical error rate for distributed operations, and that ``upgrading'' an encoding prior to distributed operations and having a cache, as part of node architecture, for qubits can be useful for distributed operations.
item.dc:creator: Seng W. Loke

item.title: Quantum Tsallis Entropy Estimation: Near-Optimal Bounds and High-Precision Improvements
item.description: arXiv:2610.22983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimating statistical properties of probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistics and theoretical computer science. We develop quantum algorithms for estimating the $q$-Tsallis entropy $\mathrm{H}_q^{\mathrm{Tsa}}(P) =\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n p_i^q-1}{1-q}$ when $0<q<1$, given purified quantum query access to a distribution $P$ on $[n]$. When $0<q\leq \frac{1}{2}$, we provide a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\rbra{\left(\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\frac{1}{2q}}}$, which is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. When $\frac{1}{2}<q<1$, we introduce a two-stage simultaneous probability estimation procedure, yielding a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{n^{\frac12+\frac{1}{2q}}}{\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2q}}}+\frac{n^{1-q}}{\varepsilon}\right)$, which improves the result given by Chen et al. (ICALP 2026) when $\varepsilon=O\rbra{n^{1-2q}}$.
item.dc:creator: Chengshen Gao, Zongxing Xiong, Lvzhou Li

item.title: Discrete time crystals and classical logic gates in coupled open Dicke models
item.description: arXiv:2610.23043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of coupled discrete time crystals (DTCs) in the coupled Dicke model or Dicke dimer (DD) with dissipation. By numerically simulating the mean-field dynamics of the system, we show that coupling two DTCs decreases their oscillation amplitude following a transient relaxation period. For sufficiently strong coupling, the coupled DTCs become unstable, resulting in the system relaxing towards the normal phase (NP). We demonstrate that the relaxation time diverges near the critical coupling strength, suggesting a continuous phase transition. Using the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA), we explore how the dynamics are affected by the introduction of quantum fluctuations. We also consider a scenario in which an NP is briefly coupled to a DTC, seeding the NP to transform into a DTC that is either synchronized or anti-synchronized relative to the DTC. We investigate the robustness of this phenomenon in the presence of noise. Using these results, we propose a scheme to perform NAND and NOR operations with three DTCs by sequentially coupling the input and output sites. We identify the parameter regimes in which the logic gate architecture remains valid, and investigate how the protocol is affected by the presence of quantum fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel D. G. U, Roy D. Jara Jr., Jayson G. Cosme

item.title: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Private simultaneous quantum messages (PSQM) provide a minimal model of noninteractive secure multiparty quantum computation, yet their communication complexity for concrete functions remains poorly understood. We show that familiar total functions already exhibit both genuine quantum advantages and strong structural limitations. For three-party equality on $n$-bit inputs, which determines whether the players' $n$-bit strings are identical, we construct an entanglement-assisted protocol with asymptotic communication $(1.633\ldots)n$ qubits, whereas every perfectly correct protocol without prior entanglement requires at least $3n$ qubits. For three-bit majority, one shared GHZ state and one transmitted qubit per player suffice for perfect correctness and perfect privacy, reducing the communication from the optimal classical cost of six bits to three qubits. Three-bit AND behaves differently. No perfectly correct and perfectly private protocol exists when the players share an arbitrary three-qubit state, apply arbitrary local unitary encodings, and transmit one qubit each. However, increasing the local dimension overcomes this obstruction: one shared three-qutrit GHZ state and one transmitted qutrit per player yield a one-shot protocol with total communication $3\log_2 3$. Together with the six-bit classical lower bound, this gives a strict quantum communication advantage. More generally, for every $k\geq 3$, we construct a perfectly correct and perfectly private one-shot protocol for $k$-bit AND using one qudit of dimension at most $k$ per player, and hence at most $k\log_2 k$ qubits in total.
item.dc:creator: Harumichi Nishimura

item.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions in the Extended Agassi Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.23096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in the extended Agassi model following sudden quenches of same level pairing ($\Sigma$), monopole-monopole ($\chi$) and cross level pairing ($\Lambda$) strengths. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the non-equilibrium dynamics through the Loschmidt echo and intensive return-rate function. Quenches across equilibrium phase boundaries produce cusp-like structures in the return rate that shows non-analyticities with increasing system size. Equilibrium finite size to large scaling identifies the $\chi$-driven transition as a second order phase transition similar to mean-field, Dicke, and Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) models critical behaviour with the exponent of the order parameter $\beta \simeq 1/2$, while the $\Sigma$- and $\Lambda$-driven transitions are first order. We further characterize the associated dynamical singularities through a local scaling exponent $\alpha$, with $\alpha_\chi \simeq 2/3$, $\alpha_\Lambda \simeq 1/3$, and $\alpha_\Sigma \simeq 3/2$ of all three parameters. The distinct scaling behaviours across the parameter channels show that dynamical criticality is not determined solely by the equilibrium order of the transition, revealing multiple dynamical scaling regimes. These non-analyticities are associated with the Fisher zeros of the Loschmidt amplitude, which cross the real time axis at critical times and the time derivatives of the return-rate function to characterize the order of DQPTs within the extended Agassi model.
item.dc:creator: Ritesh Kumar Palai, Rajiv Kumar, Venktesh Singh, Sunil K. Mishra

item.title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.23111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact symmetry at self-duality. We apply this framework to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain with two collective Lindblad channels exchanged by Kramers--Wannier (KW) duality. A strong $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry divides Liouville space into four parity sectors, while the defect acts nontrivially only in the even-even sector. At self-duality, the KW defect imposes a momentum-resolved selection rule on Liouvillian Jordan blocks. Modes with different Liouville momenta or KW-defect eigenvalues cannot form a common exceptional Jordan block. For a three-site chain, a global R\'enyi-2 KW asymmetry dynamically identifies the self-dual conditions. At the same time, the spectral structure exhibits both a semisimple degeneracy and a self-dual exceptional point with a perturbation-selective response. These results extend non-invertible dualities to Markovian quantum dynamics and establish a symmetry-based selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan structures.
item.dc:creator: Ying-Cheng Yang, Jhen-Dong Lin, Yueh-Nan Chen

item.title: Sample-Based Quantum Linear Solver and Bounds on Krylov-State Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.23138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To solve linear systems $Ax=b$, we propose a sample-based quantum linear solver combining quantum Krylov-state sampling with classical variational diagonalization. Rather than simulating the cost Hamiltonian $H_b(A)=A^\dagger(I-|b\rangle\langle b|)A$, we measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ generated by the original Hermitian operator $A$ in the computational basis. We then classically diagonalize the projected cost Hamiltonian to reconstruct an approximate solution. Using a representation of $A^{-1}|b\rangle$ as a linear combination of quantum Krylov states, we derive lower bounds on computational-basis sampling probabilities from solution amplitudes. We establish support-discovery guarantees for finite nonnegative-time grid sampling and signed-time sampling, which permits both positive and negative evolution times. The former bounds the maximum evolution time, whereas the latter improves ideal shot complexity at the cost of occasional long evolutions. For a condition-number bound $\kappa$ on $A$, a lower bound $\beta_L$ on the solution probability weight of each of $L$ target basis states, and failure probability $\delta$, signed-time sampling achieves $O(\kappa^2\beta_L^{-1}\log(L/\delta))$ shots, matching a worst-case lower bound up to constants within an evolution-only observation model in a specified parameter regime. Finally, we analyze the effects of finite-length qDRIFT compilation and circuit reuse on sampling and derive an infidelity bound for the reconstructed solution.
item.dc:creator: Byeongyong Park, Keunhong Jeong, Doyeol Ahn

item.title: Controlled PROP: Theory and Applications to Quantum Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2610.23192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Control is a fundamental concept in quantum and reversible computational models. It enables the conditional application of a transformation to a system, depending on the state of another system. We introduce a general framework for diagrammatic reasoning featuring control as a constructor. To this end, we provide an elementary axiomatization of control functors, extending the standard formalism of PROPs to controlled PROPs. As an application, we show that controlled PROPs facilitate diagrammatic reasoning for quantum circuits. In particular, they admit a simple and complete axiomatization involving at most three qubits, whereas in the standard PROP setting, completeness necessarily requires axioms involving arbitrarily many qubits.
item.dc:creator: No\'e Delorme, Simon Perdrix

item.title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: E. J. W. Koh, Rongjie Zhang, Dzmitry Matsukevich

item.title: Anticommuting Displacement Operators, Exact Pauli Algebras,and the Singlet State from the Oscillator Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.23264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an explicit construction of a pair of anticommuting Weyl displacement operators for a harmonic oscillator and use bounded functional calculus to obtain exact dichotomic representatives of the Pauli algebra. Two independent oscillators provide commuting Pauli algebras for Alice and Bob. The standard singlet-sector projector, written entirely in terms of these bounded oscillator observables, is then applied to the two-oscillator vacuum. We show explicitly that the projected vacuum has nonzero norm, so its normalization is well defined, has the exact singlet correlations, and reaches the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt2$ for the usual Bell--CHSH settings. We also clarify that the construction generally realizes a singlet sector with multiplicity, rather than selecting a unique vector in the full oscillator Hilbert space, and we compare the construction with the older pseudospin approach to continuous-variable Bell tests.
item.dc:creator: S. P. Sorella

item.title: Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.23296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and its variants are leading algorithms to help solve challenging combinatorial optimization problems. QAOA maps these problems to Ising Hamiltonians such that their ground state is the desired solution. Candidate solutions are then drawn from a variational quantum circuit. The performance of QAOA hinges on a set of variational angles. However, finding good angles is an instance-specific and computationally expensive non-convex classical optimization task. Here, we learn the mapping from the problem instance to high-quality QAOA angles. Our learned models replace the per-instance optimization, that we call the solver, with a single forward pass that is several orders of magnitude faster than the solver with a near identical quality. Our models further generalize to unseen topologies such as Barab\'asi-Albert and 2D grid graphs. Experiments on quantum hardware confirm that QAOA samples with angles produced by our open-source models are indistinguishable from solver angles. Crucially, models sensitive to the topology of the problem instance increase the quality of the QAOA angles. Our work amortizes a major bottleneck in QAOA by an up-front data generation and training cost. Importantly, this cost can be amortized over time in settings where many similar problems are optimized on a regular basis, as is often the case in applications for industry.

item.title: SpinControl: Control Software for Prototyping and Benchmarking of Spin-Qubit Devices and Measurement Protocols
item.description: arXiv:2610.23316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computers require software to control the states of the qubits. As the actions on qubits grow in complexity with circuit execution, calibration, and benchmarking, the complexity of the control software grows in tandem. Spin-qubit quantum computers are at a stage where experimentalists need low-level access for tuning and calibration, and quantum algorithm researchers want high-level circuit-level access. In this article, we present the software design of SpinControl. SpinControl integrates three architectural metrics: 1) customizability, to allow prototyping devices and measurement protocols, is achieved by separating data and behaviour; 2) modularity and extensibility are achieved by separating functionalities into different components; and 3) robustness, to reliably execute quantum circuits on many qubits, is achieved by CI pipelines and input validation. SpinControl allows different types of measurements while customizing the instruments used, the pulse or circuit program executed, and the data processing. It allows building standardized experiments from measurement and analysis building blocks and executing these for calibration in a custom and conditional order. SpinControl implements these functionalities alongside robust configuration and data management, a connection to the cloud, and calibration scheduling. Pulse and circuit compilation, virtual gate matrices, as well as spin-qubit-specific GUIs integrated by SpinControl, make heavy use of software packages developed by Delft University of Technology: pulse lib, core-tools (both open source), and QConstruct
item.dc:creator: Harold B. Meerwaldt, Dani\"el P. van der Velde, Pieter T. Eendebak, Michiel J. Haye

item.title: Temperature dependence of the Casimir force between plane-layered structures: an approach based on the principle of argument
item.description: arXiv:2610.23354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the complex analysis theorem the principle of argument, a temperature-dependent formula for the Casimir-Lifshitz dispersion force of the interaction of two arbitrary plane-layered structures separated by either a vacuum gap of size d or a layer of size d consisting of an arbitrary dissipative dielectric with dispersion is derived. The formula consists of the temperature-dependent Lifshitz formula plus the temperature-dependent contour integral
item.dc:creator: Michael V. Davidovich

item.title: Bell scenarios encode classical non-causality
item.description: arXiv:2610.23367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bell and contextuality scenarios are unified within the Ac\'in-Fritz-Leverrier-Sainz hypergraph formalism, in which measurements are hyperedges. Multipartite measurements are obtained from product rules that combine independent contextuality scenarios into a single hypergraph. Several such rules exist: they are structurally distinct, yet yield the same classical, quantum, and boxworld correlations. Here, we show that this difference is not incidental, unveiling an unexpected connection. The measurements of composite Bell scenarios are exactly the process functions, the deterministic classical communication protocols that may be non-causal, i.e., lack a definite causal order without generating paradoxes. Validity of a hyperedge and logical consistency of a process function are thus one and the same condition. This allows us to characterize process functions by normalization and no-signaling alone, providing transformations that generate non-causal process functions from no-communication ones. The product rules, in turn, order process functions by causal structure, from no-communication to non-causality, which yields a graphical criterion for the latter: a process function is non-causal precisely when its hyperedge is generated by the disjunctive but not the maximal product. We thereby obtain the first joint hypergraph representation of (non-causal) process functions and (nonlocal-without-entanglement) measurements, recasting classical non-causality as a non-standard way of composing black boxes.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Leitherer, Kyrylo Simonov, Ravi Kunjwal, Antonio Ac\'in, Kuntal Sengupta, Hippolyte Dourdent

item.title: Resonance crossings and diabolical points for DC electric field quantum sensors
item.description: arXiv:2610.23392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since the 1990s, experiments on double-well heterostructures have highlighted a key phenomenon: applying an external DC electric field induces pronounced wave packet oscillations at specific field strengths. \ To gain a deeper insight into this effect, a comprehensive quantitative analysis of the properties of quantum resonances near a crossing point is required. \ This approach lays the theoretical foundation for devising a quantum sensor capable of rapidly and efficiently determining whether the strength of an external DC electric field lies within a narrow target range.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Sacchetti

item.title: Quantum Sensitivity of $N$-Component Cat States
item.description: arXiv:2610.23398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend our previous study of squeezed two-component Schr\"odinger cat states to a phase-referenced single-mode family with an arbitrary number $N$ of coherent components and general relative phases. Within the established circular-state construction, we derive a closed complex overlap kernel for the ordered action of displacement, phase rotation, and squeezing, retaining exact finite-amplitude normalization. We distinguish finite-displacement orthogonality from local phase-estimation sensitivity quantified by quantum Fisher information (QFI). For equal-phase states, we compare $N=2,\ldots,9$ at a common mean photon number and include coherent-state and squeezed-vacuum benchmarks. A bound on the higher photon-number sectors establishes the fixed-energy asymptote $F_{Q,N}=4\bar n(N-\bar n)+o(1)$. Its leading term agrees with the known QFI of a vacuum--$N$-photon superposition. The resulting decrease of the ideal local quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound does not establish unlimited attainable precision: prior phase information, sample size, phase-reference resources, optical loss, state preparation, and measurement choice remain relevant.
item.dc:creator: Ranjit Singh, Alexander E. Teretenkov

item.title: Quantum Circuits for Variable-Coefficient Vlasov Dynamics via Schr\"odingerisation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional Vlasov equations present promising use cases for quantum simulation, but their transport coefficients must be implemented coherently in order to preserve a compact quantum representation. We develop explicit Schr\"odingerised circuits for prescribed external field Vlasov dynamics without classical field updates. In 1D1V, velocity-dependent streaming is compiled directly from the encoded velocity register, while a non-linear cubic field is evaluated using reversible fixed-point arithmetic. For fixed polynomial degree, the field workspace scales linearly with the coordinate register width, while the field evaluation subroutine has polynomial depth. As a proof of concept, we simulate a minimal coupled 3D3V anharmonic Penning system and realise mixed electric-field terms and transverse magnetic coupling on a six-dimensional phase space in agreement with classical calculations. Resource analysis shows approximately linear growth with the number of time steps, while identifying the auxiliary register as the dominant depth bottleneck. Structured preparation and register recovery of the auxiliary state reveal an interplay between loading cost and readout. Together, our algorithm demonstrates a fully coherent quantum simulation of high-dimensional Vlasov dynamics with variable coefficients and identifies the practical resource costs that must be controlled for large-scale quantum implementation.
item.dc:creator: Fong Yew Leong, Dax Enshan Koh, Wei-Bin Ewe, Qiubo Chen, Zhun-Yong Ong

item.title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.23415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying quantum neural networks (QNNs) on sparse hardware requires preserving task accuracy while reducing compiler-induced two-qubit gates, SWAPs, and depth. We present ConQUESTA (\underline{C}onstrained \underline{Qu}antum \underline{E}ntangler \underline{S}election with \underline{T}opology \underline{A}wareness), a post training pruning framework that combines task saliency with compiler cost, screens candidate entanglers, and searches complete pruning masks under an explicit accuracy constraint. Unlike one-shot ranking, each mask is transpiled as a whole across multiple coupling topologies. Across 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit QNNs and eight model seeds at 55% pruning, ConQUESTA achieves mean resource reductions of 61.6% on Breast Cancer, 72.0% on Digits01, and 82.2% on Iris, exceeding the strongest matched simple baseline by 3.5, 1.7, and 8.9 percentage points, respectively. Fixed-mask recovery raises feasibility from 16/24 to 22/24 runs. In a fixed-k=4 scaling study on a scaling probe of 4 to 12-qubits, the raw mask space grew from 495 to 12.1M while the evaluated masks increase only from 189 to 305. Resource-weight changes alter depth/routing priorities with at most a 0.44-point mean validation shift.
item.dc:creator: Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

item.title: Cayley access models for matrix functions: reachable class and cost
item.description: arXiv:2610.23429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how to compute $f(A)b$ on a quantum computer, where $A$ is Hermitian. When $f$ is nonsmooth or has localized difficulty in the spectrum, classical numerical linear algebra approximates it with rational functions rather than polynomials. We propose the Cayley transform, parameterized by $\sigma \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\gamma > 0$, as an alternative to the standard quantum access model. The two parameters let one concentrate accuracy where $f$ is difficult, which standard models can achieve only by raising the polynomial degree globally. This transformation converts Hermitian matrices to unitaries, allowing generalized quantum signal processing to apply Laurent polynomials bounded on the unit circle. We compare three access models (block encoding, matrix exponential, and Cayley encoding) in terms of query complexity and of the cost of their circuit realization. When the difficulty of $f$ is localized in the spectrum, the Cayley encoding reduces the required degree by a factor of three to four, and it represents the shifted resolvent exactly at degree one. For spectral projectors, the standard models cannot reach the target accuracy at fixed degree, because their approximants cannot concentrate resolution near the discontinuity. Realizing the Cayley encoding from a block encoding requires solving a shifted linear system, whose cost offsets its query-complexity gain over the standard models. For structured matrices arising in practice, however, low-depth circuits for the encoding can be constructed directly, and the gain is preserved at the circuit level.
item.dc:creator: Gianna M. Del Corso

item.title: A Fibre-Integrated SPDC Heralded Single-Photon Source Using Zn-Indiffused PPLN Ridge Waveguides at Telecom Wavelengths
item.description: arXiv:2610.23499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a fully fibre-integrated source of broadband polarisation-entangled photon pairs at telecom wavelengths based on a commercially available Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide incorporated within a Sagnac interferometer. Operating across the full degenerate SPDC spectrum using pump-suppression filtering only, the source exhibits a measured bandwidth of approximately 67 nm. Strong non-classical correlations are observed, with an average two-photon interference visibility of 96.9 +/- 0.2 %, a fidelity to the Phi + Bell state of 78.1 %, and a CHSH Bell parameter of S = 2.501 +/- 0.005. We further explore the effect of increasing source brightness on Bell-state performance, revealing the limitations of accidental-corrected metrics in high-flux operating regimes.

item.title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
item.description: arXiv:2610.23507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian inference enables self-consistent plasma parameter inversion in tokamak integrated data analysis by fusing multi-source diagnostics. However, under nonlinear Gaussian likelihoods, finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate typically relies on sampling methods whose high computational overhead precludes real-time plasma control. To address this bottleneck, we propose a Bayesian inversion framework using a Coherent Ising Machine (CIM)-a quantum computing architecture based on coupled degenerate optical parametric oscillators (DOPOs). With native all-to-all connectivity, the CIM directly maps the negative log-posterior potential onto a spin Hamiltonian and leverages quantum vacuum fluctuations for rapid state-space search during pitchfork bifurcation. Validated on plasma current profile inversion for the EAST tokamak, this method achieves a single-run solution time of approximately 1 ms. Although current qubit limits necessitate a block-wise iterative scheme that prevents full real-time execution today, rapidly scaling quantum hardware offers a clear pathway toward real-time tokamak control.
item.dc:creator: Zijie Liu, Wenchao Liu, Wenxin Li, Anzhe Jiang, Hongdong Zhu, Qi Gao, Yin Ma, Hai Wei, Yao Huang, Yuehang Wang, Kai Wen, Jiangang Li

item.title: Temperature dependence of a warm ensemble based memory on quantum communication rates
item.description: arXiv:2610.23536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The success of long-distance quantum communication will hinge on quantum repeater nodes equipped with robust and scalable quantum memories. Such memories must possess specific operating characteristics to make these nodes practical. An attractive option for these memory devices is an atomic warm vapor system operating under the conditions of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT). These systems are easy to implement and require relatively low equipment overhead. A key metric in atomic-based quantum memory performance is optical depth, as it is closely tied to the strength of light-matter coupling. Here, we simulate and measure the optical depth-based performance of an EIT quantum memory using a warm atomic vapor cell. We then translate the simulated and measured optical depth and efficiency metrics into expected entanglement distribution rates. Our analysis evaluates the feasibility of these memories in optical quantum repeater nodes, which are essential for robust long-distance quantum communication.

item.title: Electrostatic Limits on Quantum Spatial Search
item.description: arXiv:2610.23560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a quantum walker cannot search a two-dimensional lattice in Grover's $O(\sqrt N)$ time, resolving the long-standing open question posed by Aaronson and Ambainis in 2003. A walker that hops between neighbouring sites of an $L\times L$ lattice, $N=L^2$, needs $\Omega(\sqrt{N\log N})$ local steps at least to find a marked vertex, even with unlimited memory and free queries. Hence, Tulsi's algorithm is asymptotically optimal. Our proof rests on a surprising correspondence with classical electrostatics. We treat the marked vertex as a point charge and weight the overlap between the walker's states with and without the mark by the potential drop, which vanishes where queries act. Only local steps change this weighted overlap, at a rate limited by the field energy, so the lower bound is set by the self-potential of the charge. In the plane this self-potential grows logarithmically with system size, like the Coulomb potential, leading to the extra root-logarithmic factor. Several marked vertices turn the charge into a conductor, and the lower bound depends on their arrangement through its capacitance.
item.dc:creator: Weikang Li

item.title: Improving the estimation of spin-bath parameters via initial correlations and a two-qubit probe
item.description: arXiv:2610.23582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how a second qubit can improve the estimation of spin-environment parameters when only one of the two qubits is measured. Both qubits are coupled to a common spin bath through the exactly solvable central-spin model, in which populations and coherences both evolve. Because the bath operator coupled to the qubits commutes with the bath Hamiltonian, the environment induces no effective interaction between the qubits. Without initial correlations or direct inter-qubit coupling, the two-qubit probe therefore performs exactly like a single qubit. When initial system-environment correlations are included, preparing the second qubit reshapes the environment statistics in a parameter-dependent way, and the measured qubit reads out this imprint. This improves the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the coupling strength by factors of 3-4 relative to a correlated single-qubit probe, and by more than an order of magnitude relative to an uncorrelated one. For temperature estimation, the improvement reaches a factor of about 8. A direct Ising coupling does not help by itself, but the advantage persists in its presence. We also derive the classical Fisher information for arbitrary projective measurements and identify the measurement that saturates the QFI, which in general lies out of the equatorial plane of the Bloch sphere.
item.dc:creator: Anila Khan, Huzaifa Amjad, Rizwan Abbas, Ali Raza Mirza

item.title: Certifying information flow in multi-agent behaviours
item.description: arXiv:2610.23631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study which input-output behaviours of several agents can be produced by a declared communication schedule, that is, a fixed sequence of senders, recipients, message alphabets, and output times, together with shared randomness. Since a schedule admits only finitely many deterministic protocols, membership is a linear program, and an infeasible target is excluded by a separating inequality. Under explicit operational assumptions, we prove that the affine hull of the achievable behaviours is described exactly by the equalities stating that each joint output statistic depends only on the inputs that can reach the agents involved, so that a violated equality identifies both the statistic and the missing input. One binary message per event already attains this affine hull, so message capacity restricts which behaviours are achievable without being visible to any equality. We apply the result to one-bit broadcast and relay hierarchies for two and three agents, and to low-order projections of the local polytope.
item.dc:creator: M. Haider Akbar, Onur Pusuluk, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

item.title: Partially isophase electro-magnetic configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Separation of variables in Schr\"{o}dinger equation allows an infinite-dimensional family of physically distinct field configurations that are dynamically indistinguishable in one selected sector, labeled by a conserved quantum number, while differing in all others. We call such a symmetry a partial isophase symmetry. Two main examples are considered: axially symmetric magnetic backgrounds (a rigid spectral flow of the Fock--Darwin oscillator, purely magnetic isophase families, and a two-channel extension) and a Cartesian slab geometry (magnetic barriers in two-dimensional electron gases, treated in the Appendices). We further discuss the consequences of this symmetry for the inverse spectral problem and consider its quasiclassical counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Andrey M. Pupasov-Maksimov

item.title: Delta-sigma noise shaping for low-resolution quantization in Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum key distribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.23654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-resolution digital-to-analog conversion can simplify continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD) transmitters, but coarse quantization increases excess noise and can generate data-correlated spectral replicas. We demonstrate digital delta--sigma modulation (DSM) for low-resolution waveform generation in Gaussian-modulated CVQKD. In a 500-MBaud CVQKD system over 20~km of fiber, 3-bit second-order DSM achieves an estimated asymptotic secret key rate of 46.38~Mbps at an oversampling ratio of 12, whereas uniform quantization yields no positive rate. With 4-bit second-order DSM, the rate reaches 50.11~Mbps, approximately 97\% of the 12-bit reference. A noise model combining the DSM noise-transfer function with matched filtering guides the sampling-rate and signal-band design for effective noise suppression. We also identify a phase-conjugate spectral replica arising from third-order intermodulation between the pilot tone and quantum signal, and evaluate its key-rate penalty using a linear-replica security model. At 3-bit resolution and an oversampling ratio of 24, first-order DSM reduces the experimentally estimated leakage-mode strength by approximately four orders of magnitude. Together, our findings establish the security boundaries and operating conditions of DSM, providing design guidance for low-resolution CVQKD transmitters.
item.dc:creator: Wenjun Fan, Zhenlin Zhao, Dawei Wang

item.title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.23692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum kernels are among the most promising methods in quantum machine learning, providing a natural way to embed data into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces via quantum circuits and capturing non-linear relationships in data. Their learning behaviour is governed by the function class they represent, which is formally characterized by the structure of the associated Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS). However, a theoretical characterization of this function class, and of how it depends on the choice of feature map and its hyperparameters, is still lacking. In this work, we focus on the Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) feature map and derive a Fourier representation of the associated RKHS generators as finite sums of trigonometric functions evaluated on polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies determined by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter. This representation identifies three bandwidth regimes with qualitatively distinct expressive properties from localised, through multimodal, to periodic. Numerical experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure, across data dimensions and feature-map configurations, reproduce the three regimes in both supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, benchmarked against a classical Gaussian kernel. These results make the relationship between expressivity and data structure explicit for IQP kernels: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data, which provides a criterion for selecting the bandwidth when the periodic or multimodal structure of data is known.
item.dc:creator: Valeria Repetto, Stefano Melchionna, Romina D'Aurizio

item.title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.23695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Hayakawa

item.title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
item.description: arXiv:2610.23827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Future quantum networks will rely on control-plane decisions such as routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation. Each decision depends on a timely and reliable estimate of the quality of the entanglement that a candidate path can deliver, with end-to-end fidelity as a central metric. Inspired by the optical-networking experience with quality-of-transmission (QoT) estimation, this article asks when a quantum controller should compute fidelity analytically, simulate it, or learn a surrogate model. The optical analogy is useful but incomplete: optical QoT estimation often predicts a scalar transmission margin, whereas quantum QoT estimation must account for probabilistic entanglement generation, random memory waiting times, decoherence, state consumption, and measurement constraints that can make fidelity a stochastic target. We propose a compute/simulate/learn framework for quantum QoT estimation and illustrate it with a simulation-based proof of concept. Our study shows that analytical composition can be sufficient in simple regimes, that simulation becomes necessary when stochastic memory effects shape the delivered fidelity distribution, and that lightweight learned surrogates can approximate simulator labels at much lower runtime cost for online control. We close with open challenges for deployment, including stochastic targets, sim-to-real transfer, data-generation cost, physics-informed learning, and generalization beyond individual paths to full network topologies.
item.dc:creator: Anis Bekri, Amar Abane, Van Sy Mai, Abdella Battou, Saddek Bensalem

item.title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
item.description: arXiv:2610.23832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss an effective paradigm of utilizing AI agents to better compile quantum circuits when one can constrain bottleneck subroutines to have some form of classically verifiable structure. For example, when critical subroutines are composed exclusively of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement based uncomputation, one can efficiently simulate execution for classical inputs. This property facilitates efficient certification of approximate circuit synthesis via a form of fuzz testing, provided suitable assumptions on the input distribution. While this pattern was recently exploited to improve quantum cryptanalysis circuits, here we highlight the flexibility of the broader approach by discussing three important applications. (1) The computation of $1/\sqrt{x}$ that bottlenecks real space simulations of the Coulomb operator such as those important for modeling inertial confinement fusion reactors. (2) The decoding of Reed-Solomon codes which bottlenecks the decoded quantum interferometry algorithm when used to approximately solve the optimal polynomial intersection problem. And (3) the quantum look-up tables and controlled application of Givens rotations that bottleneck the most performant quantum algorithms for simulating chemistry in second quantization. We discuss reference implementations of these algorithms and how they can be constrained and verified in the interest of seeding a Kaggle competition designed to accelerate AI-based research into the optimization of their compilation.
item.dc:creator: Tanuj Khattar, Nicholas C. Rubin, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Guang Hao Low, Ryan Babbush

item.title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
item.description: arXiv:2610.23834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood. We study data reuploading quantum circuits with two distinct inputs: a signal that varies between samples and a fixed, task-defined spectral query that specifies how the signal should be probed. We show that encoding the query can change the circuit's hypothesis class over the signal by modulating how its existing signal frequencies are combined, without introducing new sample-dependent information. This mechanism matches tasks built on nonuniform Fourier transforms, whose evaluation frequencies specify the query and whose sampling positions guide its encoding. We examine this connection in a classification task inspired by synthetic aperture radar, where acquisition geometry determines a query for classifying unfocused spectral patches before image formation. Across small-scale spectral and radar-like tasks, aligned queries improve learning from limited data over parameter-matched circuits with mismatched or absent queries. These results provide a route from known spectral task structure to the design and validation of inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits.
item.dc:creator: Felix Frohnert, Adri\'an P\'erez-Salinas, Sebastian Lange, Marcus Schwaebisch, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Vedran Dunjko

item.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
item.description: arXiv:2610.23840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum error correction can suppress logical errors exponentially with code distance when physical noise is below threshold. Realizing this on hardware requires tight coordination among quantum gates, mid-circuit measurements, and qubit coherence. Device variation, noise asymmetry, and correlations across space and time complicate the translation of these capabilities into logical error suppression. Here, we study rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor. Performance varies across tested processor placements, which we attribute to differences in qubit quality. We optimize the code by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an XX echo on data qubits during ancilla readout. Compared with standard readout without reset or echo, the optimized syndrome extraction circuit reduces the median per-round logical error rate by factors of 3.8 in the X basis and 1.4 in the Z basis. In memory experiments of up to 150 rounds, the distance advantage weakens, alongside long-lived correlations that may reflect a persistent error component. Under our optimization recipe, increasing the protected distance from 3 to 6 while holding the other distance fixed reduces the per-round logical error rate from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory. The corresponding error-suppression factors under maximum-likelihood decoding are 1.68 and 1.85. These results connect circuit compilation and optimization to surface-code memory performance and limitations, and motivate QPU and QEC circuit codesign for fault-tolerant quantum computing primitives on current cloud hardware.
item.dc:creator: Shuwen Kan, Aaron Hoyt, Sean Garner, Ethan Vo, Adrian Harkness, Rod Rofougaran, Zefan Du, Chenxu Liu, Norm Tubman, Ying Mao, Samuel Stein

item.title: QMBL: the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard. A live record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2610.22387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In condensed matter physics, scientists explore phase diagrams of matter through various methods (analysis, numerics, experiment) and achieve consensus when enough methods agree. The quality of variational results for quantum many-body ground states is mainly judged by energy values and respective errors. Here, we present QMBL, the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard (https://www.qmbl.org), serving as the energy layer of the scientific consensus. It is a maintained, interactive record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians. The latest release v0.4.0 holds 1434 energies on 395 instances of six model families and collects all of the community's efforts into one view. Of those instances 153 have no exact solution and any new record serves as a direct improvement to an open science problem. They are the targets of a companion benchmark, QMBL: Open Problems.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Zerweck, Juan Carrasquilla

item.title: Semiclassical Analysis of Wave Dynamics via Wigner Transforms: Applications to the Quantum Harmonic, Anharmonic, and Dirac Oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2610.22414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this Master's thesis, we give a pedagogical introduction to the semiclassical analysis of wave dynamics in single-band and multi-band systems. We show how the semiclassical evolutions of Wigner functions can approximate the dynamics of wave packet centers and wave packet deformations. Three systems of increasing complexity are considered: the quantum harmonic oscillator and the quantum anharmonic oscillator as single-band systems, and the Dirac oscillator as a two-band system. We explain the origins of the first-order semiclassical corrections (Moyal, Littlejohn-Flynn, and Berry) in the equations of motion and examine their effects on predictive accuracy. Another focus is set on the conditions for validity of the semiclassical analysis. For both the quantum anharmonic and the Dirac oscillators, a dimensionless parameter controlling the accuracy of the approximation is identified. In multi-band systems, the formalism applies only to states within a single adiabatic subspace, which, for the Dirac oscillator, corresponds to an energy branch. This motivates the construction of single-branch almost coherent states: approximately Gaussian wave packets formed by superpositions of states from a single energy branch. Their centers undergo oscillations with an aperiodic envelope. These states enable comparison between semiclassical Wigner function evolution and the commonly used Sundaram-Niu formalism. We show that semiclassical Wigner function evolution captures deformation-related dynamics, including the initial decay of oscillations, which the Sundaram-Niu formalism cannot describe by construction. Additionally, exact quantum evolution reveals partial relocalization of these single-branch almost coherent states, a phenomenon that cannot be captured by the semiclassical evolution.
item.dc:creator: August Burg

item.title: Dilaton-Axion Wormhole Partition Function Away from the BPS Endpoint
item.description: arXiv:2610.22429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: I determine the leading finite-radius correction to the two-boundary response of a charged axion wormhole near its BPS endpoint. With $\delta=a_*^2$, exact radial matching in a product axion--dilaton/saxion system gives a boundary eigenvalue that vanishes as $O(\delta)$ and an off-diagonal Hessian entry of order $O(\delta^2)$. Their combination produces a cross-boundary covariance linear in $\delta$, with a negative first sub-leading correction on the branch studied here. I determine the semiclassical range in which the quadratic approximation remains controlled and identify the first finite-radius angular resonance, $\delta^2\log(\delta/\delta_0)$. Under a uniform rescaling of all active charges, the coefficient of the linear cross-boundary response scales as the inverse square of the charge scale. I then average the inverse response over the chiral Gaussian ensemble describing the BPS endpoint. Boundary reduction preserves the hard-edge index. Multiplication by the matched BPS sector weight converts the normalized response into the leading finite-radius two-source coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Jong Rey

item.title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22501v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a J\"uttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Silva

item.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.22614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $\mu$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.
item.dc:creator: Shelby Klomp, Shafaq Gulzar Elahi, Scott Grudichak, Chethn Galla, Zhiyuan Wang, Mark Nguyen, George Winstone, Katarina Boskovic Guy, Emma Derrick, Maddox Wroblewski, Jacob Sprague, Andrew Laeuger, Jackson Larsen, Nancy Aggarwal, Shane L. Larson, Andrew A. Geraci

item.title: Universal Threshold Laws for Dipolar Evaporation of Molecular Fermi Gases
item.description: arXiv:2610.22639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fermi statistics suppress the elastic collisions that rethermalize a Fermi gas during evaporative cooling, creating a fundamental low-temperature bottleneck for producing quantum degenerate gases. We show that, for shielded single-component ultracold dipolar molecular Fermi gases in the Wigner threshold regime, this bottleneck is governed by universal threshold laws fixed by the effective dimensionality of the gas. In this regime, Fermi suppression of rethermalization scales quadratically with temperature in 3D but only linearly in 2D. Consequently, the thermalization-to-loss ratio is more favorable in 2D than in 3D, and these results suggest that 2D geometries are better suited for reaching deep degeneracy. We also present ab initio close-coupling calculations that agree well with experimental measurements on Fermi degenerate gases of KRb molecules, supporting our conclusions.
item.dc:creator: Kevin B. Xu, John L. Bohn, Reuben R. W. Wang

item.title: Area Theorems for Quantum Error Correction
item.description: arXiv:2610.22710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) and generalized EXIT (GEXIT) area theorems provide fundamental conservation laws that connect the rate of classical codes to the performance of maximum-a-posteriori decoding on binary memoryless channels. In this work, we generalize these area theorems to quantum error correction. We first develop a coset-entropy formalism for nested linear codes, where the message specifies a coset and encoder randomization selects a codeword within that coset. The area under the resulting coset (G)EXIT function equals the normalized dimension of the quotient. For stabilizer codes, the measured syndrome restricts the Pauli error but does not always determine its logical effect, and the remaining uncertainty is an entropy over logical correction classes. We show that this entropy equals a classical coset entropy associated with the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it.
